hunt.justification: Exploited-in-the-wild zero-day vulnerabilities targeting core OS security mechanisms (MOTW and Defender) represent a high risk of undetected initial access and evasion. A negative result confirms the estate is either patched or currently unexploited.

meta.name: Windows Shell and .NET Framework Zero-Day Bypasses

related.reason: This hunt specifically targets the October 2026 zero-day registry triggers; general .NET hijacking requires deeper process-to-module correlation.

meta.analysis: A single detection rule for these CVEs only confirms a vulnerability is present. This hunt pivots to rare registry stack-counts and MOTW alternate data stream contents to provide the behavioral evidence an analyst needs to differentiate exploitation from legitimate software updates.

scenario.summary: This campaign involves the exploitation of two zero-day vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-96951 to bypass Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) security features via malicious files or websites, and CVE-2026-108398 to bypass Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) by registering malicious .NET assemblies for loading by protected processes.

meta.rationale: The scoping step identifies vulnerable devices by their provider UID. Resolve these UIDs to hostnames using hb_devices and then paste them into the scope_hosts parameter to focus the behavioral analysis.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has exploited a Windows Shell MOTW bypass to execute malicious web downloads without warning, or has achieved stealthy persistence by registering a rare .NET assembly that evades Defender signature checks.

hunt.name: Windows Shell and .NET Framework Zero-Day Bypasses
hunt.description: This hunt targets two zero-day vulnerabilities from the October 2026 Patch Tuesday: CVE-2026-96951 (Windows Shell MOTW bypass) and CVE-2026-108398 (.NET Framework assembly hijacking). The hunt identifies vulnerable hosts and then looks for behavioral indicators of exploitation, specifically monitoring for rare registry modifications within the .NET Framework and CLSID paths, and hunting for files in user-writable directories that contain Zone.Identifier tags indicating an untrusted internet origin. An agent triage step settles the findings across these independent surfaces.

config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, status FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE instr(',' || '{{cve_ids}}' || ',', ',' || cve_uid || ',') > 0
config.description: Locate devices reporting the specific zero-day vulnerabilities in their latest vulnerability scan.
config.expected_signal: A list of device UIDs susceptible to the targeted bypasses. Silence indicates either no vulnerabilities were found or the scanner has not yet been updated with October 2026 logic.

primitive_config.label: Identify vulnerable hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, status FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE instr(',' || '{{cve_ids}}' || ',', ',' || cve_uid || ',') > 0
primitive_config.expected: A list of device UIDs susceptible to the targeted bypasses. Silence indicates either no vulnerabilities were found or the scanner has not yet been updated with October 2026 logic.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(reg_target) AS target, reg_value_data, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\\software\\microsoft\\.netframework%' OR LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\\software\\classes\\clsid%') AND activity_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Stack-count registry writes to .NET Framework paths to identify rare assembly registrations that may indicate hijacking.
config.expected_signal: A registry value seen on very few hosts. Legitimate software updates may appear, but a rare path or value data is the primary indicator of assembly hijacking.

primitive_config.label: Rare .NET assembly registrations
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(reg_target) AS target, reg_value_data, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\\software\\microsoft\\.netframework%' OR LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\\software\\classes\\clsid%') AND activity_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: A registry value seen on very few hosts. Legitimate software updates may appear, but a rare path or value data is the primary indicator of assembly hijacking.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_name, file_path, process_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\downloads\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\temp\\%') AND LOWER(file_contents) LIKE '%zoneid=3%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find files downloaded from the internet (ZoneID=3) into user folders that may have bypassed security warnings.
config.expected_signal: Files with MOTW metadata in user-writable paths. The presence of such files on vulnerable hosts suggests a failure of the MOTW security feature.
